# Texas AI Docket

> A public, fact-checked record of decisions about artificial intelligence in Texas. Every entry carries verbatim quotes from the sources it rests on, and at least one primary source. Every numeral is computed from data, never written by a person.

This record may be read, indexed, cited and quoted. Attribution to the Texas AI Docket with a link to the page is requested. No crawler is blocked. Every decision also exists as Markdown at the same path plus index.md, and the whole record is one fetch at /llms-full.txt.

## Start here

- [The record, every tracked decision](https://texasaidocket.com/record/)
- [Questions answered from the record](https://texasaidocket.com/questions/)
- [Every source a claim was checked against](https://texasaidocket.com/sources/)
- [Texas Grid Watch, the daily ERCOT record](https://texasaidocket.com/grid/)
- [Texas Water Watch](https://texasaidocket.com/water/)
## Questions, by what is being asked

Each page answers one kind of question about every decision on the record.

- [What each decision is](https://texasaidocket.com/questions/what-it-is/): The record's own summary of every entry it carries.
- [Who decides](https://texasaidocket.com/questions/who-decides/): The body holding the pen on each decision.
- [How the public can take part](https://texasaidocket.com/questions/taking-part/): The room each decision is being made in, and what that room allows.
- [Where a comment window is open](https://texasaidocket.com/questions/open-comment/): The decisions taking written comment right now.
- [Where in Texas each one applies](https://texasaidocket.com/questions/where-in-texas/): Counties and metros, from the geography on the record.
- [What has been decided](https://texasaidocket.com/questions/decided-or-pending/): Settled, pending or withdrawn, for every entry.
- [What happens next](https://texasaidocket.com/questions/what-happens-next/): The next dated step on each decision, counted against today.
- [When each one started](https://texasaidocket.com/questions/when-it-started/): The earliest date on every entry's record.
- [What kind of decision each one is](https://texasaidocket.com/questions/kind-of-decision/): The topic each entry is filed under.
- [What sources back each one](https://texasaidocket.com/questions/sources-behind-it/): How many documents stand behind an entry, and how many are primary.
- [Which are on the ERCOT grid](https://texasaidocket.com/questions/on-the-ercot-grid/): Inside or outside the interconnection that covers most of Texas.
- [When each one was last checked](https://texasaidocket.com/questions/last-checked/): The date every fact on an entry was last verified against its source.

## Open right now

Decisions a member of the public still has a dated way into.

- [Dallas Public Safety Committee sets a briefing on the police Flock plate reader program](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0116/): The Dallas City Council Public Safety Committee has put an update on the Dallas Police Department's Flock automated license plate reader program on its September 8th, 2026 agenda.
- [Federal comment window open on adding AI questions to the American Time Use Survey](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0016/): The Bureau of Labor Statistics has proposed adding questions about artificial intelligence to the American Time Use Survey. Public comment is open under the Paperwork Reduction Act. Comments close September 8th, 2026.
- [Federal commodities regulator opens comment on trading derivatives whose underlying commodity is compute](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0118/): The Commodity Futures Trading Commission published a request for comment on August 21st, 2026 asking what a designated contract market should weigh before listing derivatives with compute as the underlier.
- [Governor Abbott directs the utility commission and ERCOT to audit every data center in the interconnection queue before any advances](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0072/): Governor Greg Abbott issued a directive on August 3rd, 2026. It tells the Public Utility Commission of Texas and ERCOT to run a verification and audit of every data center moving through the interconnection process.
- [Governor orders state agencies to pause funding for Flock plate reader cameras](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0111/): The Governor's office ordered every Texas state agency to pause funding for Flock automated license plate reader cameras, and confirmed the order on August 28th, 2026.
- [League City City Council ordered a November 3rd special election on whether police may keep using automated license plate reader cameras](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0048/): On August 11th, 2026 the League City City Council approved Ordinance No. 2026-27 on first and final reading. The ordinance orders a special election on November 3rd, 2026.
- [PUCT open meeting calendar published as a live feed through mid 2027](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0024/): The Public Utility Commission publishes its open meetings and public comment deadlines as a machine readable feed. Every entry is marked open to the public and names the room.
- [PUCT opens the first five year review of the ERCOT system-wide offer caps, with comments due September 17th](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0107/): The Public Utility Commission of Texas has opened Project 59550, the quinquennial review of the system-wide offer cap programs under 16 TAC Section 25.509(d).
- [Pflugerville orders a November election on charter amendments, one of them a section on the city's use of artificial intelligence](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0075/): The Pflugerville City Council approved on second reading on August 11th, 2026 an ordinance ordering a special election on November 3rd, 2026 on amendments to the city's home rule charter.
- [Senate Economic Development cancels its September 3rd hearing on AI and the Texas workforce and resets for September 22nd](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0109/): The Senate Committee on Economic Development carries an interim charge on preparing the Texas workforce for artificial intelligence.

## The whole record, by beat

### Data centers

- [A statewide poll finds most Texas voters oppose a data center in their own community for a second survey running](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0105/): The Texas Politics Project at the University of Texas at Austin polled 1200 registered Texas voters from August 5th to 13th, 2026. It reported that 57 percent oppose the construction of a data center in their community.
- [Angelina County Commissioners Court adopts Resolution 010-26 asking the Legislature for authority over data centers](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0044/): Angelina County Commissioners Court voted unanimously on July 14th, 2026 to adopt Resolution 010-26. It asks the Texas Legislature to grant counties specific powers over large scale industrial development that local...
- [Archer County Commissioners Court unanimously denies a tax abatement for a Dynamo Ventures data center](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0043/): Archer County Commissioners Court voted unanimously on June 22nd, 2026 against a tax abatement for a data center proposed by Dynamo Ventures LLC. More than 30 residents packed the courthouse to oppose the incentive.
- [Austin City Council takes up a resolution to amend the land code for data centers](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0115/): A resolution on the Austin City Council's August 27th, 2026 agenda directs staff to begin amendments to City Code Title 25, the Land Development Code.
- [Austin City Council takes up a resolution to write data centers into a land development code that has no definition of one](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0106/): Item 61 on the Austin City Council's regular meeting agenda for August 27th, 2026 asks the council to approve a resolution. It would initiate amendments to Title 25 of the City Code, the Land Development Code.
- [Brazoria County Commissioners Court adopted a resolution stating conditions it wants on data center development](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0052/): On June 9th, 2026 Brazoria County Commissioners Court adopted a measure on data center development. Its own agenda system records it as a resolution about data centers and related facilities in Texas.
- [Brazoria County Commissioners Court voted 5 to 0 to deny the reinvestment zone that four data center and power plant abatement applications depended on](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0051/): Brazoria County Commissioners Court opened and closed a public hearing on the creation of Brazoria County Reinvestment Zone No. 26-01 on March 10th, 2026. The court then refused to create the zone. Commissioner David R.
- [Brazos County Commissioners Court assigns the RELLIS data center tax abatement to ThisWay Global after the original developer's bankruptcy](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0088/): Brazos County posted a Tax Code Section 312.207 notice that its Commissioners Court would consider assigning the tax abatement agreement for the RELLIS Campus data and research center.
- [Carson County Commissioners Court approves a phased tax abatement agreement with Fermi America for the Project Matador HyperGrid campus](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0046/): Carson County Commissioners Court approved a tax abatement agreement with Fermi America for the Project Matador HyperGrid campus in the Texas Panhandle.
- [City of Taylor's notice of an amended Compal tax abatement is no longer posted, and no outcome is published](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0027/): The City of Taylor published a public notice for its City Council. The council would consider an Amended and Restated Tax Abatement Agreement with Compal Technology, Inc. and PDC TP 01 LOT A LLC.
- [Comptroller's JETI current agreements list contains no data center project](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0013/): The Texas Jobs, Energy, Technology and Innovation Act is the state's school district property tax incentive program. The Comptroller publishes the current executed agreements.
- [Corpus Christi City Council directed staff to write a zoning amendment prohibiting data centers in every zoning district and to prepare a moratorium process](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0050/): The Corpus Christi City Council passed a motion on July 21st, 2026 as agenda item 18, moved by Council Member Gilbert Hernandez and seconded by Council Member Carolyn Vaughn.
- [Denton City Council takes up a data center moratorium resolution and a schedule of the public hearings it would require](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0087/): An agenda item asked the Denton City Council to approve a resolution on a moratorium. It covers the acceptance and processing and approval of applications for data center development inside the city limits.
- [El Paso City Council adopted a letter asking Governor Abbott to clarify his data center directives](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0034/): The El Paso City Council approved and adopted a letter to Governor Greg Abbott seeking clarification on his directives on data center development throughout Texas.
- [El Paso City Council adopts a Data Center Policy Framework requiring a Special Permit for hyperscale projects](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0033/): The El Paso City Council voted on July 20th, 2026 to adopt a Data Center Policy Framework. The resolution came through a City Council Work Session and passed on a motion by Representative Boyar Trejo.
- [Governor Abbott directs the utility commission and ERCOT to audit every data center in the interconnection queue before any advances](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0072/): Governor Greg Abbott issued a directive on August 3rd, 2026. It tells the Public Utility Commission of Texas and ERCOT to run a verification and audit of every data center moving through the interconnection process.
- [House State Affairs held an interim hearing on data center development and the proposed 765 kV transmission lines](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0078/): The Texas House Committee on State Affairs met on August 19th, 2026 on two interim charges. The first directs it to study the development of data centers in Texas and to review the regulatory framework governing that...
- [Killeen Planning and Zoning Commission voted against a conditional use permit for a $30 million ONMINE data center](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0032/): The Killeen Planning and Zoning Commission voted against a conditional use permit for a $30 million data center proposed by the company ONMINE. It voted at its regular meeting on April 27th, 2026.
- [Laredo City Council declined a data center moratorium, and its direction to write permanent rules has reached three agendas with no recorded action](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0037/): Laredo City Council declined to impose a temporary moratorium on data center permits at its meeting on July 27th, 2026.
- [Lubbock County Commissioners Court passes a non binding disclosure resolution on large scale industrial development, four to one](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0045/): Lubbock County Commissioners Court passed a non binding resolution on August 10th, 2026. It asks large scale industrial developers to disclose expected water use, electricity use and infrastructure impacts before...
- [PUCT told an Armstrong County AI data center to shed its whole load, then left those conditions in place](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0108/): The Public Utility Commission of Texas approved a net metering arrangement in Docket 59220 on July 24th, 2026. It lets a second AI data center complex share the point of interconnection and the settlement meter of...
- [San Angelo writes data centers into its zoning code and makes them a conditional use only](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0066/): San Angelo created Section 430 of its zoning ordinance, the first full land use rulebook for data centers in West Texas.
- [Temple Planning and Zoning Commission takes up a Unified Development Code amendment that would require a Conditional Use Permit for every future data center](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0026/): The Temple Planning and Zoning Commission has three data center items on its August 17th, 2026 agenda. The central one is a set of proposed Unified Development Code amendments.
- [Tom Green County Commissioners Court declines a Precinct 4 moratorium on data centers and large energy projects](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0070/): The Tom Green County Commissioners Court voted not to pursue a temporary moratorium on large scale energy and data center development in Precinct 4.
- [Wichita Falls Planning and Zoning Commission approves a conditional use permit for a DataNovaX data center on Airport Drive](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0041/): The City of Wichita Falls Planning and Zoning Commission approved a conditional use request from DataNovaX. It lets the company put a data center inside an existing building at 2236 Airport Drive on the north side of...
- [Williamson County Commissioners Court granted Compal USA Technology a Chapter 312 abatement for a Georgetown server service center](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0029/): The Williamson County Commissioners Court approved a Chapter 312 tax abatement incentive agreement for Compal USA Technology Inc. on April 15th, 2026.
- [Young County Commissioners Court receives the Project Saltworks tax abatement application and ratifies a developer funded escrow for consultants](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0042/): Young County Commissioners Court formally received a tax abatement application from Headwaters Site Development for the Project Saltworks data center campus at the courthouse in Graham on August 10th, 2026.

### Defense and federal

- [Federal comment window has closed on NRC reactor licensing and siting modernization](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0015/): The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has proposed a wholesale revision of its reactor licensing, safety oversight and siting rules. The revision is being carried out under an executive order directing reform of the agency.
- [Federal commodities regulator opens comment on trading derivatives whose underlying commodity is compute](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0118/): The Commodity Futures Trading Commission published a request for comment on August 21st, 2026 asking what a designated contract market should weigh before listing derivatives with compute as the underlier.

### Health and education

- [A generative AI platform at UTMB reached the UT System Regents only on its third amendment, at $9,850,000, and now covers all seven health institutions](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0094/): The University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston contracted in December 2024 for a platform giving it a secure way to work with generative artificial intelligence models.
- [House Public Health held an interim hearing on artificial intelligence use in health care](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0079/): The Texas House Committee on Public Health met on August 20th, 2026 on a charge about clinical artificial intelligence.
- [Houston ISD carried an artificial intelligence board policy to a second reading](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0053/): Houston Independent School District has a proposed local board policy numbered CQD(LOCAL) covering technology resources and artificial intelligence. The item was introduced on March 20th, 2026.
- [Houston Methodist put an imaging AI in front of its radiologists and says out loud that it is imperfect](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0101/): Houston Methodist rolled out a suite of AI imaging tools across the system, starting with a small group of users before widening it.
- [National Science Foundation names UT El Paso in the first round of CyberAICorps Scholarship for Service awards](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0039/): The National Science Foundation announced the first awards under its CyberAICorps Scholarship for Service program on July 28th, 2026. The University of Texas at El Paso is on the list.
- [The University of Texas at Austin requires every course syllabus to state its AI policy](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0117/): The Office of the Executive Vice President and Provost requires a Course Artificial Intelligence Policy in every syllabus every semester. The policy has to name one of three designations.
- [UT Austin puts a computer science and AI course in the core every undergraduate takes](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0100/): The University of Texas at Austin published a new Core Curriculum on August 13th, 2026 that names Computer Science and AI among the foundational courses.
- [UT Southwestern says AI now does most of the grading on its medical students' clinical exam notes](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0102/): UT Southwestern Medical Center built a process that reads and grades the post encounter notes students write after their objective structured clinical examinations.
- [UT System Regents put the first billion dollars of the UT Dell Medical Center into the capital program](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0095/): The Board of Regents approved adding the first phase of the UT Dell Medical Center in Austin to the capital improvement program. It acted at its August 12th, 2026 meeting.
- [UTMB moved its Epic health record into Microsoft's cloud and named advanced technologies as the reason](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0082/): The University of Texas Medical Branch migrated its electronic health record from servers it runs itself onto Microsoft's Azure platform, and announced the move on August 13th, 2026.

### Land, water and permitting

- [Amarillo City Council authorizes a twenty year water supply agreement selling city water to Fermi America's Project Matador](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0047/): Amarillo City Council voted five to nothing on first reading to authorize a water supply agreement with Fermi America, then took the required second reading later that month.
- [Blanco-Pedernales Groundwater Conservation District signed a resolution asking the Legislature to clarify district authority over data centers](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0060/): The Blanco-Pedernales Groundwater Conservation District board met on April 16th, 2026 and signed Resolution No. 20260416-1 requesting legislative clarification on the regulation of data centers.
- [Fort Worth City Council unanimously began a 90 day data center moratorium and adopted grid filing requirements over one dissent](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0062/): The Fort Worth City Council took three data center votes on August 11th, 2026. Members unanimously approved the first steps toward a 90 day moratorium on accepting, processing and approving new data center applications...
- [Harlingen Waterworks System board approves an effluent water supply agreement with RGV Property LLC for a proposed data center](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0038/): The City of Harlingen Waterworks System board of directors approved a water supply agreement with RGV Property LLC for a supply of effluent water.
- [Hays County Commissioners Court adopted a 180-day emergency water review period for high water use developments and created a review board](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0028/): The Hays County Commissioners Court approved a resolution on June 23rd, 2026 establishing a 180-day emergency water protection review period for high water use development applications, including data centers.
- [San Angelo City Council caps data center cooling water by ordinance](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0065/): San Angelo passed Ordinance 2026-078, which adds Section 11.02.043 to the city water service rules. It puts hard numbers on how much city water a data center may take for cooling.
- [San Angelo sets reporting rules for data center coolant discharged into the city sewer](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0067/): San Angelo adopted Ordinance 2026-076, which adds a data center subsection to the city's prohibited discharges rule.
- [San Marcos City Council voted 4 to 3 to define data centers in its land development code and make them ineligible citywide](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0061/): The San Marcos City Council voted on June 16th, 2026 to define data centers in the city's zoning rules and make them ineligible for development anywhere inside the city.
- [TCEQ canceled the Carson County public meeting on Fermi Equipment Holdco's new air permits and says it will be rescheduled](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0057/): The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality had scheduled a public meeting for August 24th, 2026 at the Panhandle High School Auditorium. It concerns proposed new air quality permits for Fermi Equipment Holdco, LLC.
- [TCEQ canceled the San Antonio notice and comment hearing on Vantage Data Centers TX11's air permit O4791](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0058/): The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality had set a notice and comment hearing for August 17th, 2026 in San Antonio. It concerns air permit O4791 held by Vantage Data Centers TX11, LLC.
- [TCEQ has four data center air permit applications posted with published public notices, including Crusoe's two Texas campuses](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0063/): TCEQ's pending new source review page lists air permit applications whose notices are open to the public. Four of them are data centers.
- [TCEQ issues preliminary decision and opens comment on Crusoe's gas power plant at the Abilene data center campus](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0064/): The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality's executive director finished technical review and drafted a permit for an electric power generation facility at 615 Farm-to-Market Road 2404 outside Abilene.
- [Tarrant Regional Water District says it has signed no water supply contract for a data center and that the Cedar Creek request was withdrawn](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0059/): The Tarrant Regional Water District publishes a standing page on data center raw water requests after developers approached it about supply from the Cedar Creek system.
- [Texas Water Development Board denied a petition to give data centers their own water demand category and adopted the 2027 State Water Plan the same day](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0056/): The Texas Water Development Board took up a petition for rulemaking on July 23rd, 2026. It asked the agency to project water demand for data centers and crypto mining as a standalone industrial category.

### Power and the grid

- [El Paso City Council amends its state legislative agenda to seek protection for residential ratepayers from data center utility costs](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0035/): On June 23rd, 2026 the El Paso City Council directed the City Manager to amend the city's 90th Session State Legislative Agenda.
- [Grid operator weighs a year's grace for data center cooling equipment on ride-through rules](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0114/): A revision request pending at the Electric Reliability Council of Texas concerns the grid's ride-through requirements. It would give a large computational load up to 365 days after its in-service date to comply.
- [PUCT Docket 59029, Oncor application for a second 765 kV line across ten west Texas counties](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0076/): Oncor Electric Delivery has applied to amend its certificate of convenience and necessity to build the Longshore Switch to Drill Hole Switch transmission line. The application covers ten named counties in west Texas.
- [PUCT Docket 59315, Oncor application for a 765 kV transmission line across 22 counties](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0003/): Oncor Electric Delivery has applied to amend its certificate of convenience and necessity to build the Dinosaur Switch to Longshore Switch transmission line.
- [PUCT Project 58000, rulemaking to update ERCOT transmission cost recovery, comment deadline reached](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0001/): The Public Utility Commission of Texas is amending its wholesale and investor owned utility retail transmission cost recovery rules for the ERCOT region.
- [PUCT Project 58482, proposed new rule on Large Load Demand Management Service, open for comment](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0002/): The Public Utility Commission of Texas has proposed a new rule governing demand management service for large electric loads. The proposal for publication creates a new Section 25.521.
- [PUCT open meeting calendar published as a live feed through mid 2027](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0024/): The Public Utility Commission publishes its open meetings and public comment deadlines as a machine readable feed. Every entry is marked open to the public and names the room.
- [PUCT opens the first five year review of the ERCOT system-wide offer caps, with comments due September 17th](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0107/): The Public Utility Commission of Texas has opened Project 59550, the quinquennial review of the system-wide offer cap programs under 16 TAC Section 25.509(d).
- [Reeves County Emergency Services District No. 2 takes up a Chapter 312 abatement for a gas plant built to run data centers](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0068/): A small emergency services district in Pecos noticed a public hearing to accept a tax abatement application from Energy Forge One LLC under Chapter 312 of the Texas Tax Code.
- [Utilities Code limits how the PUCT may direct ERCOT, and bars verbal directives](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0007/): Texas law restricts the channels through which the Public Utility Commission may order ERCOT to act. A verbal directive is prohibited outright.
- [Utility commission approves a 765 kilovolt line from Somervell County to Howard County](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0112/): The Public Utility Commission of Texas approved an amendment to Oncor's certificate of convenience and necessity for a new 765 kilovolt transmission line.

### Research and science

- [Energy Department research arm funds a Houston led team using AI to design magnets that avoid imported rare earths](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0124/): Rice University published on September 1st, 2026 that the Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy awarded a three year grant to a coalition led by the University of Houston.
- [Federal comment window open on adding AI questions to the American Time Use Survey](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0016/): The Bureau of Labor Statistics has proposed adding questions about artificial intelligence to the American Time Use Survey. Public comment is open under the Paperwork Reduction Act. Comments close September 8th, 2026.
- [Four Texas campuses took roles in the Energy Department's AI for science program](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0103/): The Department of Energy announced the recipients of its Genesis Mission in Washington on July 22nd, 2026. UT Austin leads two projects and partners on three more.
- [NSF awarded Prairie View A and M a grant to let AI split up the grid optimization problem across processor cores](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0080/): The National Science Foundation made an award to Prairie View A and M University on August 11th, 2026 under its HBCU Excellence in Research program.
- [NSF awarded UT Austin a grant to replace hand written robot safety rules with a model trained on demonstrated safe behavior](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0081/): The National Science Foundation made an award to the University of Texas at Austin on August 13th, 2026 under its Foundational Research in Robotics program.
- [NSF funds a Rice laboratory where a model designs the experiment and a robot runs it, bookable from anywhere](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0098/): The National Science Foundation award to William Marsh Rice University funds READINESS, a cloud accessible robotic laboratory for synthesizing electronic and quantum materials.
- [National Science Foundation awards Rice University a cooperative agreement for a self driving laboratory that designs its own semiconductor experiments](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0085/): The National Science Foundation obligated a cooperative agreement to William Marsh Rice University for a test bed called READINESS.
- [National Science Foundation awards Texas A and M a national user facility where robots and artificial intelligence design and test new metal alloys](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0086/): The National Science Foundation obligated a cooperative agreement to the Texas A and M Engineering Experiment Station for the Autonomous Robotic Metallurgist Materials Innovation Platform.
- [National Science Foundation backs a Texas A&M tool that screens whether an alloy can exist before anyone makes it](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0122/): Texas A&M's College of Engineering published on September 4th, 2026 that the National Science Foundation is funding PhaseForge.
- [National Science Foundation funds Rice to let AI propose numerical algorithms only where a proof checker certifies them](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0093/): The National Science Foundation made a standard grant to William Marsh Rice University in Houston on August 17th, 2026.
- [National Science Foundation funds UT San Antonio and Texas A&M to adapt large language models on machines that can't afford to run them](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0092/): The National Science Foundation made two matched standard grants on August 14th, 2026. They fund a subspace optimization framework for resource efficient and private fine tuning of large language models.
- [National Science Foundation funds a five year human and robot co-adaptation center at UT Austin](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0104/): The National Science Foundation made award 2535195 to the University of Texas at Austin on August 25th, 2026. It funds a Science and Technology Center on human and robot co adaptation.
- [National Science Foundation funds an open access robot run alloy laboratory at Texas A&M that outside researchers may book](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0090/): The National Science Foundation made a cooperative agreement to the Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station in College Station. It funds the Autonomous Robotic Metallurgist Materials Innovation Platform.
- [The Army funds a Rice research center on antenna arrays that carries AI as one of six disciplines](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0099/): The United States Army Research Office established a five year research center at Rice University for secure sensing, imaging and communications.
- [The National Science Foundation puts the national AI research resource into standing operations, co-run from Austin](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0121/): The National Science Foundation established the NSF National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource Operations Center on September 1st, 2026.
- [The Texas A&M System's shared AI supercomputer enters the world list at number 66](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0119/): VISION is the Texas A&M University System's shared AI computing platform. The June 2026 TOP500 list credits it to the System rather than to one campus and records a measured Linpack result of 34.82 petaflops against a...
- [UT Austin funds four fusion seed grants and says in its own release that the AI method offers limited guarantees](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0123/): The Institute for Fusion Studies, the Oden Institute and the Cockrell School jointly funded four fusion seed grants announced on August 31st, 2026.
- [UT System Board of Regents approved a School of Computing at UT Austin uniting computer science, information, statistics and data sciences](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0031/): The University of Texas System Board of Regents approved the creation of a School of Computing at The University of Texas at Austin on February 19th, 2026.
- [UT System Board of Regents approves $25 million to finish San Pedro II for UTSA's College of AI, Cyber and Computing](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0040/): The University of Texas System Board of Regents approved $25 million in Permanent University Fund support for San Pedro II. The money completes the build-out for UT San Antonio's College of AI, Cyber and Computing.

### State policy

- [Amazon selects Austin for a factory building the robotics systems used in its warehouses, and the mayor says no incentives were requested](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0084/): Amazon announced a new manufacturing facility in Austin that will produce the robotics systems used in its fulfillment operations.
- [DIR must run an AI regulatory sandbox letting state agencies test systems outside normal rules](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0009/): The Department of Information Resources is required to establish a program letting eligible public entities contract with registered vendors to test AI systems before deployment.
- [Houston-Galveston Area Council put AI consulting services on its HGACBuy purchasing catalog under contract AI05-26](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0054/): HGACBuy is the cooperative purchasing program run by the Houston-Galveston Area Council. It publishes an active contract numbered AI05-26 titled AI Consulting Services.
- [Pecos-Barstow-Toyah ISD's JETI agreement for the Energy Forge One power plant is executed and posted](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0069/): The Texas Comptroller now lists application J0022 among current agreements under the Jobs, Energy, Technology and Innovation Act. It pairs Energy Forge One LLC with Pecos-Barstow-Toyah ISD in Reeves County.
- [Senate Economic Development cancels its September 3rd hearing on AI and the Texas workforce and resets for September 22nd](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0109/): The Senate Committee on Economic Development carries an interim charge on preparing the Texas workforce for artificial intelligence.
- [Senate Transportation held its August 25th hearing on how driverless vehicles are being deployed under SB 2807](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0077/): The Senate Committee on Transportation posted notice of a public hearing for August 25th, 2026 in the Capitol. One of three interim charges covers the deployment of autonomous vehicle technology authorized by SB 2807 of...
- [Senate Water, Agriculture and Rural Affairs has held both sittings on data center cooling water and published no recommendation](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0096/): The Senate Committee on Water, Agriculture and Rural Affairs carries an interim charge directing it to examine how much water high consumption cooling technologies use. The charge names data centers.
- [SpaceX will build the Terafab semiconductor plant in Grimes County on a state grant and two school district agreements](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0071/): Governor Greg Abbott announced on August 6th, 2026 that SpaceX will construct a vertically integrated semiconductor fabrication plant in Grimes County.
- [State technology agency publishes how it is implementing the four AI laws of the 89th Legislature](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0113/): The Texas Department of Information Resources published an account on August 14th, 2026 of how it is implementing the artificial intelligence laws passed by the 89th Legislature.
- [Statute requires state agencies and local governments to post standardized notice of AI systems](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0025/): Every state agency and local government that deploys a public facing AI system must post a standardized notice on the related applications, websites and public computer systems.
- [TRAIGA in force as Business and Commerce Code Chapter 552, enforceable only by the Attorney General](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0006/): The Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act took effect on January 1st, 2026 as Chapter 552 of the Business and Commerce Code.
- [TRAIGA preempts city and county regulation of artificial intelligence](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0012/): Chapter 552 of the Business and Commerce Code supersedes and preempts any local ordinance, resolution, rule or regulation about the use of AI systems.
- [Texas Government Code Chapter 2054 carries three conflicting Subchapter S's on AI, with duplicated section numbers](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0008/): Three separate acts of the 89th Legislature each added a Subchapter S to Government Code Chapter 2054, and two of them number their sections identically.
- [Texas requires AI training for state and local government employees, and this is the first annual cycle](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0097/): House Bill 3512 of the 89th Regular Session created artificial intelligence training programs for certain employees and officials of state agencies and local governments.
- [The House committee on government efficiency is charged with studying whether the state should use artificial intelligence to find fraud in its own spending](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0089/): The Speaker's interim charges give a charge to the House Committee on Delivery of Government Efficiency. It is to study how the state can use technology to detect fraud and waste and abuse of taxpayer resources.
- [Two Texas House committees take up data centers and AI in health care on August 19th and August 20th](https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0073/): The House Committee on State Affairs met on August 19th, 2026 on a charge covering data center development in Texas. That charge names SB 6 and the large load batch study process the grid operator proposed.
